feature: An effect can be saved as a named style
summary: A shadow, a glow, a border or a blur you have tuned can be saved under a name, put on other layers from the plus on the Effects header, and re-tuned once so every layer wearing it follows in a single undo step. It is the third of the three kinds a style comes in, beside the saved colours and the saved text treatments, and it sits on the same Library shelf as both.
setup: Photonz Dev, Experiments window, release Next. It rides the same next-styles flag the saved colours and text styles are already behind, so it is on wherever they are.

try.do: Draw two rectangles on a blank canvas.
Select the first, press the plus on the Effects header, and choose Shadow. Tune the Softness and Distance until you like it.
Open the Style menu at the top of that shadow's settings and choose Save as Style. Type a name and press Return.
Select the second rectangle, press the plus on the Effects header, and choose your name from Saved effects at the bottom of that menu.
Click the style's tile on the Library's Styles shelf.
Drag the Softness slider in that section. Both rectangles change.
Press Command Z once. Both go back together.
Now drag the Softness slider on ONE of the rectangles, in the Effects list. That shadow quietly leaves the style and the app says so.

evaluate: Adding a saved effect from the plus, rather than dragging its tile onto a layer: is that where you would have looked for it?
The Style row sits at the TOP of an effect's settings, above the colour. Does it read as the thing that sets everything under it, or as one more setting?
The line under a styled row says changing any setting below takes the effect off the style, and it is showing the whole time. Is that a useful warning or is it in the way?
The shelf tiles draw the effect on a small piece of paper. Can you tell a shadow from a glow at that size without reading the name?
The style's own section names the effect once at the top ("Drop shadow, 12 pt, 40%"). Does that tell you enough, or do you want a bigger preview?
rough: Screen Recording was granted, so every shot here is a real capture of the probe window, not an offscreen render.

The style's section does not carry a border's "Follows" setting, which decides whether a ring goes round a label's letters or its box. It is the one border setting a style cannot change; a style saved from a label keeps whatever it was saved with. It was left out because it means nothing on any layer but a label and the section is already six rows.

There is no way to update a style FROM a layer you have just re-tuned. Tuning a styled effect breaks the link, which is the same rule the saved colours and text styles follow, but with an effect it is easier to want the other thing: you tune the shadow on one card and then wish every card had it. Worth watching for whether that is a real want or a habit from other tools.

A style can only be worn by an effect of its own kind, so the menu on a Shadow row lists only saved shadows. That is on purpose (a row titled Shadow must not become a border), but it means the row's menu is empty until you have saved something of that kind, and the only hint about where the others are is the plus.

The shelf tile is a picture drawn in SwiftUI rather than the renderer's own answer, so it approximates: an inner shadow and an inner glow are drawn as a soft band inside the plate rather than composited the way the canvas does it.
